title: Adaptive prefetch credits and cache-escrow fallback for graceful OOM recovery
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Spiky traffic and long-context requests cause unpredictable GPU memory pressure. Current heuristics sometimes trigger abrupt OOMs or overly conservative throttling that hurts latency/quality. This ticket designs and implements a coordinated mechanism that prevents hard OOMs while preserving as much output fidelity as possible.
goal: Introduce a runtime-level 'prefetch credits' budget and a cache-escrow protocol that: (1) bounds per-request memory contracts, (2) enables safe spill/snapshot to host for low-priority KV segments, and (3) provides a graceful, observable fallback ladder from full-fidelity model -> slim quantized model -> partial-response with structured rerun. Aim is to reduce hard OOMs by 90% on stress tests while keeping P50 latency increase < 10% for typical workloads.
acceptance_criteria: No hard OOMs observed in synthetic stress test (10k concurrent short and long context mixes) for 24h run
End-to-end degradation ladder executes within SLA: fallbacks return responses within configured latency SLOs for each tier
Empirical cost/latency tradeoff dashboard added to Console with token-level memory attribution
Automated unit + integ tests covering prefetch credit exhaustion, escrow snapshot restore, and hedged retry flows
Rollout gated by a canary (5% traffic) with auto-rollback on >3% customer_impact metric breach
technical_approach: Prefetch credits: each request declares a soft memory contract (contract_bytes) derived from expected KV hits and sequence length; runtime doles out prefetch credits per-GPU slot. Credits are charged as prefetches and released on decode completion.

Cache-escrow: low-priority KV segments (older prefixes, large attention keys) can be 'escrowed' to pinned host memory snapshots with a bounded restore cost. Escrow policy uses LRU-weighted eviction with cohort tagging to avoid hotkey thrash.

Per-request graceful degradation policy: on credit shortfall, runtime first trims prefetch (partial KV miss), then progressively switches to a lower-fidelity model variant (quantized or distilled) via a 'ladder' configured per-route, finally returning a structured partial response with explicit missing-context indicators and automated rerun hooks.

Hedged/replicated retry: for requests likely to trigger heavy restore, issue a speculative secondary request to a warm slim-model instance; the first satisfying response wins (hedging TTL tuned by latency profiles).
Observability: instrument per-token memory attribution, prefetch credit accounting, escrow restore latency, and ladder transitions; surface as new Console charts and trace tags.
Safety: ensure rollback semantics for escrow restore failures (fall back to soft-fidelity response) and circuit-breaker to avoid cascading restores under fleet-wide pressure.

progress_updates: 2026-02-22: Kickoff design review with runtime, infra, and product. Agreed on contract_bytes approach rather than fixed token quotas.
2026-02-28: Prototype credit tracker implemented (local loopback) and validated against synthetic workload; initial leak conditions fixed.
2026-03-04: Cache-escrow prototype for host snapshots integrated with async restore; restore latency median 35ms for small segments, 210ms for large segments (need tuning).
2026-03-08: Hedged retry design finalized; will use dynamic TTL based on P95 restore latency from dashboard.
risks_and_mitigation: Restore latency can exceed SLO and cause double-load: mitigate by conservative cohorting and throttled restores with backpressure tokens
Escrow to host memory increases host RAM usage: mitigation via per-GPU escrow quotas and eviction policies bound by resident set caps
Complexity increases operational surface: mitigation by adding feature flags, graceful off switch, and thorough runbook including metrics alerts and automated rollback
test_plan: Unit tests for credit accounting edge cases (concurrent charge/release, double-free scenarios)
Integration tests using CI cluster with mixed-length sessions to validate ladder behavior
Stress test (10k connections) with varied sequence distribution to measure OOM reduction and latency impact
Chaos test: simulate host snapshot corruption and verify fallback responses and alerting
rollout_plan: Feature gated behind runtime flag and per-team toggle
Canary: enable for 5% of traffic on non-enterprise fleets for 72 hours
Monitor: memory OOM rate, ladder transition rate, escrow restore latency and customer_impact
Gradual ramp: 5% -> 25% -> 100% with 24h hold and automated rollback on threshold breach
observability_goals: Per-request memory contract and actual memory used (per-token attribution)
Prefetch credit utilization heatmap by route
Escrow restore latency histogram and failure rate
Ladder transitions per-1000 requests and fidelity loss metric
dependencies: model-catalog: provide slim model variants with quantized weights (ENG-12059)
notes: This approach favors predictable graceful degradation over hard failures. It is intentionally conservative on restores during fleet-wide stress. For enterprise customers with dedicated capacity we will provide an opt-in 'aggressive restore' profile that expands escrow quotas.
Follow-up ticket planned to add per-customer SLA-aware ladder tuning and paid-priority restore lanes.
